summary: Controls how many reasoning tokens the model may spend before answering. Higher effort can improve complex planning, coding, and verification, but increases latency and billed output-token use. The catalog validates the request against the selected model because supported levels and defaults are not uniform.
combines: Supported on: gpt-5 family and o-series only. `gpt-5.6-sol` documents none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max. `gpt-5.5` documents none/low/medium/high/xhigh (no `max`). `gpt-5.1` documents none/low/medium/high. `minimal` is the gpt-5.0-era lowest tier. Non-reasoning models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1) reject the `reasoning` object.
Directly drives cost and latency: reasoning tokens are billed as output tokens, so `xhigh`/`max` can multiply the bill several times over for the same visible answer.
Must be paired with a generous `max_output_tokens`, since the reasoning budget is drawn from it.
`effort: "none"` makes some models behave like non-reasoning models; on `gpt-5.1` that is reportedly the state in which `temperature` becomes acceptable.
Not every listed value is valid on every model — an unsupported tier is a 400.
note: Per-model allowed levels and defaults are synchronized, including max on GPT-5.6 and restricted medium/high/xhigh on Pro models.
